scope.description: Per-instance command decision agreement across recovery in a five-node volatile configuration tolerating up to two crash failures.
assumptions: Static N=5,F=2 and distinct participant identities
At most one crash in the selected history; no Byzantine inputs or restart
Messages are actual emitted bytes and dispatched in a schedule allowed by per-type protocol channels
excluded: Automatic termination or a numeric recovery deadline

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: Bound allocation to eight instances per row; omit autonomous peer listeners and protocol event loops, preserving their selected dispatch semantics.
Buffer sockets and explicitly separate receipt from per-type dispatch; model one peer crash using the Alive eligibility change.
Run the actual executor only at node3 for its known hole; use unbuffered recovery queue to suspend it at the next request and synchronize cleanup.
Emit command JSON and status snapshots; target code and message fields are not replaced.

plan_uncertainties: No isolation of one necessary root cause among interacting recovery/formation mechanisms.
The schedule delays pending message types and suspends the executor at a reachable request boundary; production autonomous scheduling is not replayed wall-clock for wall-clock.
No client-visible/application endpoint or universal recovery result is inferred.
